chunks: Indeed, I find myself detesting the man for whom means of earning become difficult, so he lies on his back and says, 'O Allah, provide for me,' while abandoning going forth in the land and seeking from the bounty of Allah; while the ant comes out from its hole seeking its sustenance.

key_terms.فَضْلِ اللَّهِ: the bounty and provision of Allah
key_terms.يَنْتَشِرَ فِي الْأَرْضِ: to go forth through the land seeking opportunity

ai.seo_question: Does Islam teach that a person must work and seek livelihood instead of only making du'a for provision?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches that seeking livelihood requires effort and that merely making du'a without pursuing lawful means is blameworthy. Imam Abu Jaʿfar عليه السلام emphasizes that even the ant strives for its provision, showing that reliance upon Allah must be joined with action.
